consistent_criteria.rule: Criteria must not assign the same concrete case to conflicting typed outcomes.
consistent_criteria.source_excerpt: True and false must describe opposing outcomes of the same proposition. Check exclusions against the positive definition; an example must not satisfy both merely because one side uses a broader term.

identify_question_references.rule: Point instructions at the specific state values and entities they judge when more than one reference could fit.
identify_question_references.source_excerpt: When a question is about one of those parts, name it in the `instructions` with a dot-and-index path to its key, including the backticks.

identify_state_component_entity.rule: A needed state value must identify which entity or subject it describes when several could fit.
identify_state_component_entity.source_excerpt: Keep role, entity, unit and timeframe checks separate when their answers can differ.

identify_state_component_timeframe.rule: A needed state value must identify its timeframe when different timeframes would change the answer.
identify_state_component_timeframe.source_excerpt: Keep role, entity, unit and timeframe checks separate when their answers can differ.

identify_state_component_unit.rule: A needed state value must identify its unit when different units would change the answer.
identify_state_component_unit.source_excerpt: Keep role, entity, unit and timeframe checks separate when their answers can differ.

identify_state_reference_target.rule: Select the exact supplied item, entity, baseline, or comparison target when several targets could fit.
identify_state_reference_target.source_excerpt: Explicit paths make it clear which parts of a structured state should inform each judgment.

instructions_align_with_criteria.rule: Treat criteria as an extension of the instruction; align their subject, direction, and answer meaning.
instructions_align_with_criteria.source_excerpt: **Instead:** treat the criteria as an extension of the instruction. Align the two using clear and precise language.

make_state_comprehensible.rule: Review the supplied state's language separately from question wording; a needed component can have one meaning yet remain difficult to parse.
make_state_comprehensible.source_excerpt: A question can have one meaning yet use nested negation or unclear clause attachment.

model_judges_code_acts.rule: System One returns typed judgments; code owns generation, tools, control flow, and side effects.
model_judges_code_acts.source_excerpt: Keep control flow, deterministic rules, and side effects in code.

name_state_component_role.rule: Name and structure a state component so its semantic role in the judgment is identifiable.
name_state_component_role.source_excerpt: Use an object for most requests so each part of the state has a descriptive name and its relationships remain clear.

name_the_judged_property.rule: State which entity and property, relation, category, or ordered degree the typed answer represents.
name_the_judged_property.source_excerpt: Write it as a clear, specific question, or as a statement for the model to judge.

noul_is_one_proposition.rule: Use Noul for the probability that one stated proposition is true; use Choice for one selection and Score for degree.
noul_is_one_proposition.source_excerpt: Ask one yes/no question per Noul. If a question has two conditions, such as "Is the customer angry and asking for a refund?", the model has to judge both at once and the value means less.

supply_case_evidence.rule: Supply the case-specific facts needed by the judgment; ordinary semantic knowledge does not replace unavailable current facts or implementation evidence.
supply_case_evidence.source_excerpt: Do not rely on knowledge stored in model weights when current information can come from your own knowledge base.

write_direct_comprehensible_questions.rule: Write instructions directly, without nested negation, unclear attachment, or avoidable indirection.
write_direct_comprehensible_questions.source_excerpt: **Instead:** write your instructions as directly as possible. When possible, identify the relevant parts of state by name.
